question: How were losses controlled in Tipam sand?
answer: Partial losses were recorded on entering Tipam sand in three nearby wells, at mud weights of 1.23–1.24 SG [1][2][3]. In OW-02, a 50 bbl LCM pill (CaCO₃ + fibre) was pumped and the mud weight was reduced to 1.18 SG; losses stopped within 6 hours [1]. OW-05 used the same approach (40 bbl LCM pill, mud weight down to 1.18 SG, 10% lower flow rate) and cured losses in about 5 hours [2]. In OW-07 an LCM pill alone did not hold and losses returned until the mud weight was cut to 1.19 SG [3]. Across these wells, an LCM pill combined with a mud weight of about 1.18 SG is what worked.

question: Which wells had stuck pipe in Barail and what worked?
answer: Two nearby wells had stuck pipe in Barail. OW-01 (2011) had differential sticking at 3,478 m after 25 minutes static on a connection and was freed after 14 hours by jarring and a freeing pill [1]. OW-04 (2016) packed off at 3,520 m after about 40 minutes of rising torque and falling ROP, and was freed after 20 hours [2][3]. In both wells the rest of Barail was drilled without sticking by holding ROP at 10–12 m/hr, running wiper trips every 150–200 m and keeping static time on connections short [1][2].

question: What cementing issues were seen on 9⅝" casing?
answer: One nearby well, OW-07, had a cementing problem on 9⅝" casing with the shoe at 3,385 m [1]. Returns were lost into Tipam sand during displacement, leaving the top of cement about 350 m below plan, and the CBL showed poor bond [1][2]. A remedial squeeze through perforations at 2,950 m restored acceptable bond after 26 hours of NPT [2]. The report recommends curing Tipam losses before the cement job and using a lighter lead slurry (1.50 SG) [1]. The completion report for OW-05 records no cementing problems on its 9⅝" casing [3].

question: What mud weight was used through Girujan in nearby wells?
answer: Girujan clay was drilled with 1.14–1.20 SG water-based mud in nearby wells [1][2][3]. OW-05 used 1.16–1.20 SG with no hole problems [1]. OW-02 used 1.15–1.20 SG and raised the weight to 1.20 SG near the base of Girujan ahead of Tipam [2]. OW-01 used 1.14–1.18 SG [3]. No losses or influx were reported in Girujan. The main caution is not to carry more than about 1.20 SG into the top of Tipam, where losses started at 1.23–1.24 SG [2].

question: Why is the current torque and ROP trend similar to OW-04 before stuck pipe?
answer: In OW-04, torque rose from about 15 to 21 kft·lbf while ROP fell from 14 to 6 m/hr over roughly 40 minutes, before the string packed off at 3,520 m [1][2]. Over the last 30 minutes, readings on NWIS-ACTIVE-01 show a similar shape: torque is up about 3 kft·lbf and ROP is down about 40%. After the incident, the OW-04 crew avoided a repeat by circulating bottoms up, back-reaming, and holding ROP at 10–12 m/hr with hi-vis sweeps [2]. This is a match on trend shape, not a certainty. Check hole cleaning and torque-and-drag before drilling ahead.

question: Was any kick or overpressure seen in deep Barail?
answer: OW-06 took a 12 bbl kick at 3,890 m MD in deep Barail while drilling with 1.32 SG mud [1]. The well was shut in and killed with the driller's method, and the mud weight was raised to 1.38 SG before drilling ahead; 19 hours were lost [1]. The completion report notes a pressure ramp starting about 60 m above the kick depth, seen as rising background gas and connection gas [2]. No other well in scope was drilled deep enough to confirm this zone, so the related alert is rule-based [2].
